Imagine a hot day, a hard run, and instead of sweat, you start leaking Coca-Cola.
Sweat is almost pure water, and it cools you by evaporating off your skin.
But cola is about one tenth sugar, and sugar doesn't evaporate.
So the water dries up, and the sugar stays behind, as a sticky, brown glaze.
Your shirt stains, your arms stick to your sides, and the glaze can slow your cooling.
Then every wasp and ant nearby smells dessert.
Skin bacteria would feast on it too, so you'd probably smell worse.
And a hard workout would sweat out nearly three cans of sugar an hour, draining your energy.
So be glad your sweat is boring. Salty water keeps you cool, not candied.
